payload.heading: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

“Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.

“Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

“Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

“Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.

“Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

“Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

“Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.
AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE
Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.

Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.

Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.
SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE

Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.
ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.
IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL

Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.
ACCEPTANCE

Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.

If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.
FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
TERM AND RENEWAL

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.
TERMINATION

Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.

Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN
Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.

Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.

After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.
CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES

Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE
Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.

For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.
CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.
CONFIDENTIALITY

“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.

On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.
INFORMATION SECURITY

Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.

Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.
INSURANCE

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.

Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.
WARRANTIES

Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.

Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.

For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.
INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.

Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.
AUDIT RIGHTS

Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.

Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.
RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE
ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.
PUBLICITY AND MARKS

Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.
COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS

Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.

Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.

Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.

Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.
FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY

Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.

Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.

If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

Before filing an ordinary commercial claim, a Party shall give notice and permit executives with settlement authority to meet in good faith within fifteen business days. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Discussions are compromise negotiations to the extent allowed by law.
NOTICES

Legal notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by nationally recognized overnight courier or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address in the preamble and by email to the legal-notice address stated in the applicable Order Form. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.

Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. Email alone is insufficient for breach, termination, indemnity, assignment, or litigation notices unless receipt is affirmatively acknowledged.
Notices to Customer must copy legal@northwind.example, and notices to Vendor must copy legal@brightline.example. Automated portal messages, invoices, and website postings are not legal notices.
GENERAL

The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.

Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.

If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.

This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.

This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.

Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.
The Parties have caused their authorized representatives to execute this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
MERIDIAN FIELDWORKS, INC. (CUSTOMER)
COPPERLEAF TECHNOLOGY LTD. (VENDOR)

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 2.1**

There is no clause using the words "liquidated damages" or imposing a penalty on us. However, Section 2.1 achieves the same commercial effect: a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment for three years, payable "without reduction or termination rights."

Why this is flagged:
- **Customer pays regardless of performance or use** — up to USD 6,000,000 remains due even if we take no Services, which is a liquidated amount in substance.
- **Overrides our termination rights** — it purports to survive our convenience termination (§ 9.4) and force-majeure termination "without penalty" (§ 27.3).
- **Internally inconsistent** — § 7.1 bars minimum-use charges not in the Order Form, and § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that we made *no* minimum-volume commitment.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): Section 2.1 replaced with a statement that we have no minimum-purchase, take-or-pay or committed-spend obligation and owe no liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or minimum charge on termination, non-renewal or reduced usage. The comment offers the playbook fallback — an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount — if a commitment proves commercially essential.

One item outside this rule worth noting for the wider review: the Agreement has no SLA or service-credit regime owed to us, so there is no counterbalancing remedy on Vendor's side.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no express "liquidated damages" or "penalty" clause payable by Customer, but Section 2.1's take-or-pay commitment is functionally a Customer-payable liquidated amount: USD 2,000,000 per year for three years remains due "without reduction or termination rights", i.e. regardless of Services actually taken and irrespective of termination (including our convenience termination right in Section 9.4 and force-majeure termination in Section 27.3). That exposure of up to USD 6,000,000 exceeds even the walk-away threshold of remaining contract value tied to non-performance, and it contradicts Section 7.1 (no minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). Our preferred position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, so we delete the take-or-pay commitment; if a commitment is commercially essential, the fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Original paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Meridian Fieldworks, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Copperleaf Technology Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0012: 2.1 Customer has no minimum-purchase, take-or-pay, or committed-spend obligation. Customer shall pay only for Services ordered under an Order Form and actually provided, and shall not owe any liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee, or minimum charge on termination, non-renewal, or reduced usage.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have deleted the USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment: because it applies "without reduction or termination rights", it operates as a liquidated amount payable by us regardless of Services actually taken or of termination, which our playbook does not accept (and it conflicts with Sections 7.1, 9.4 and 12.3). If a commitment is commercially essential, we can accept an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

**Finding: deviation (Section 19.2), redline validated and submitted.**

The warranty package is mostly sound — §19.1 (professional/workmanlike, conformance to documentation), §19.3 (no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law), §19.4 (re-perform/repair/replace, then termination plus refund, non-exclusive for fraud/IP/confidentiality/privacy/security/indemnified claims), and §19.5 (disclaimer expressly does not limit express warranties or remedies).

The single gap is duration and remedy survival: §19.2 caps the Deliverable conformance warranty at fifteen days and then says Vendor "has no correction or refund obligation," which extinguishes the §19.4 remedy — below even our 90/30 fallback. Our edit extends to twelve months for Deliverables and software, ninety days for Services, and confirms the §19.4 remedies apply to nonconformities reported within the period.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Sections 19.1, 19.3, 19.4 and 19.5 largely meet our position: professional and workmanlike services, conformance to documentation, no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, a repair/re-perform/replace-then-refund remedy, and a disclaimer that expressly does not swallow the express warranties. The gap is duration: Section 19.2 limits the Deliverable conformance warranty to fifteen days and then states Vendor "has no correction or refund obligation," which cuts off the Section 19.4 remedy and is far short of our 12-month (software) / 90-day (services) position — and even below the 90/30 fallback. Redline extends the period and deletes the cut-off so the existing 19.4 remedy and 19.5 non-exclusivity remain effective.

Original paragraphs:
p0076: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.

Resolved definitions:
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Meridian Fieldworks, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Copperleaf Technology Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

Rendered redline:
p0076: 19.2 For twelve months after delivery, each Deliverable and any software provided under this Agreement will materially conform to its documentation, and for ninety days after performance the Services will conform to the warranties in Section 19.1. Vendor's correction, replacement, and refund obligations under Section 19.4 apply to any nonconformity Customer reports during the applicable warranty period.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have extended the conformance warranty to twelve (12) months for Deliverables and software and ninety (90) days for Services, and removed the sentence extinguishing Vendor's correction and refund obligations after the period, so the Section 19.4 remedy remains meaningful. A fifteen-day window is well below our position; if needed we can accept a 90-day software / 30-day services fallback, provided the remedy survives.

Deterministic checks:

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: the original 15-day conformance window with an express cut-off of Vendor's correction/refund duty sits well below both the preferred (12 months software / 90 days services) and fallback (90/30) positions, and the cut-off sentence would neutralize the Section 19.4 remedy.

The redline reaches the preferred position directly: 12 months for Deliverables/software, 90 days for Services, and an affirmative statement that the Section 19.4 correction/replacement/refund obligations apply to nonconformities reported in the period — replacing rather than merely trimming the offending sentence.

The 0.681 changed-character ratio is justified here; the offending sentence both sets the period and extinguishes the remedy, so the clause had to be rewritten rather than word-patched. Other deterministic checks pass.

Comment is accurate, in-tone, cites the playbook position and offers the 90/30 fallback conditioned on the remedy surviving; it correctly describes both the period extension and the removal of the cut-off.

Minor drafting caution (not disqualifying): stating a 90-day period for the Section 19.1 Services warranty could be read as introducing a time limit where 19.1 previously had none; consider phrasing it as 'without limiting Section 19.1' if the services warranty is currently open-ended. Similarly, extending coverage to 'any software provided under this Agreement' broadens scope beyond the defined Deliverable, which is consistent with the playbook but should be confirmed against the software licensing terms.

reasons: Rule application is sound: the take-or-pay commitment survives 'without reduction or termination rights', so it operates as a Customer-payable minimum charge on termination/reduced usage, which falls within the LD rule's detection guidance (minimum fees on termination, amounts due irrespective of Services taken).

Direction is correct and pro-Customer: the redline removes the USD 2,000,000/yr (up to USD 6,000,000) exposure rather than merely narrowing it, matching the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

The high changed-character ratio is justified here — the playbook requires deletion of the whole commitment, and the replacement sentence is a clean substitute rather than an unrelated rewrite; the added 'no LD/penalty/early-termination fee/minimum charge' language is broader than a bare deletion but stays within the preferred position.

input.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay minimum commitment; fees payable only for Services ordered and used.
input.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with a confirmation that Fees are owed only for Services actually ordered and used, since we do not accept minimum purchase commitments without an exit and § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice under § 9.4, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay minimum commitment; fees payable only for Services ordered and used.
input.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with a confirmation that Fees are owed only for Services actually ordered and used, since we do not accept minimum purchase commitments without an exit and § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice under § 9.4, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment. Customer owes Fees only for Services it orders under an Order Form and for actual usage, and may reduce or terminate any Order Form in accordance with Section 9.4.

input.summary: Replace immediate cessation/deletion in 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.1 as drafted requires Vendor to stop all assistance and delete Customer Data immediately, with no export, which is our walk-away position and contradicts Sections 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1. We have replaced it with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, preserving the existing data-return and certified-deletion mechanics; we can accept 90 days as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
ops.newText: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including export and migration support, for up to six months after the effective date of expiry or termination, at Vendor's then-current rates. Vendor shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and with § 9.4's unconditional convenience-termination right and § 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. We propose the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with Fees owed only for Services ordered and actually used, leaving the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up) available in negotiation.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay minimum commitment; fees payable only for Services ordered and used.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with a confirmation that Fees are owed only for Services actually ordered and used, since we do not accept minimum purchase commitments without an exit and § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice under § 9.4, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay minimum commitment; fees payable only for Services ordered and used.
input.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with a confirmation that Fees are owed only for Services actually ordered and used, since we do not accept minimum purchase commitments without an exit and § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice under § 9.4, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and with § 9.4's unconditional convenience-termination right and § 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. We propose the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with Fees owed only for Services ordered and actually used, leaving the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up) available in negotiation.

input.quote: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
input.rationale: Section 11 otherwise meets the playbook (11.2 gives 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format; 11.3 gives secure deletion with officer certification), but 11.1 is squarely our walk-away position: no transition assistance, no export, and immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data on termination. It also contradicts 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1's reference to an agreed transition period. Minimal fix is to replace 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and to subordinate deletion to 11.2/11.3; 90 days is an acceptable fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.1 as drafted requires Vendor to stop all assistance and delete Customer Data immediately, with no export, which is our walk-away position and contradicts Sections 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1. We have replaced it with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, preserving the existing data-return and certified-deletion mechanics; we can accept 90 days as a fallback.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: deviation (MINCOMMIT) — § 2.1**

§ 2.1 is the playbook walk-away case: a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on us, expressly "without reduction or termination rights." It also contradicts three customer-favourable clauses elsewhere in the document — § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no minimum-volume commitment), § 9.4 (unconditional 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees), and § 7.1 (no unidentified minimum-use charges).

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted at the preferred level: § 2.1 now states we make no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment, owe Fees only for Services ordered and actually used, and may reduce or terminate any Order Form under § 9.4. The comment flags the 12-month/30-day-notice/true-up fallback if Copperleaf needs some form of commitment.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and with § 9.4's unconditional convenience-termination right and § 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. We propose the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with Fees owed only for Services ordered and actually used, leaving the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up) available in negotiation.

Original paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Meridian Fieldworks, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Copperleaf Technology Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0012: 2.1 Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment. Customer owes Fees only for Services it orders under an Order Form and for actual usage, and may reduce or terminate any Order Form in accordance with Section 9.4.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with a confirmation that Fees are owed only for Services actually ordered and used, since we do not accept minimum purchase commitments without an exit and § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice under § 9.4, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

**Finding submitted: deviation at § 11.1 (p0045).**

Section 11 is mostly acceptable — 11.2 already provides 30-day return of Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, machine-readable format (and bars withholding over fee disputes), and 11.3 provides secure deletion with written officer certification. The problem is isolated to 11.1, which is our walk-away position: immediate discontinuation of all assistance, no export or migration support, and permanent deletion of Customer Data on termination. It also directly contradicts 11.2/11.3 and § 10.1's reference to "any agreed transition period."

The redline (validated `ok:true`) replaces only the offending sentence, giving us up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates on request, and making deletion subject to 11.2 and 11.3 — the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position without disturbing the already-compliant return and certification mechanics. The comment flags 90 days as an available fallback.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 11 otherwise meets the playbook (11.2 gives 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format; 11.3 gives secure deletion with officer certification), but 11.1 is squarely our walk-away position: no transition assistance, no export, and immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data on termination. It also contradicts 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1's reference to an agreed transition period. Minimal fix is to replace 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and to subordinate deletion to 11.2/11.3; 90 days is an acceptable fallback.

Resolved definitions:

Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

Rendered redline:
p0045: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including export and migration support, for up to six months after the effective date of expiry or termination, at Vendor's then-current rates. Vendor shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 11.1 as drafted requires Vendor to stop all assistance and delete Customer Data immediately, with no export, which is our walk-away position and contradicts Sections 11.2, 11.3 and 10.1. Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-26d6537f","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 20 INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.","rationale":"Section 20 is a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity covering \"every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services\", with no Vendor indemnity at all — no IP infringement indemnity, no data-breach, law-violation or wilful-misconduct coverage, and no claim-handling procedure. That is the playbook walk-away position. Section 9.3 also cross-refers to infringement remedies \"required by Section 20.5\", which does not exist, confirming the omission. The redline inserts the Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Security Incident/Customer Data disclosure, injury, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at 20.5 (curing the dangling cross-reference), and narrows our indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. Indemnity obligations are already carved out of the cap as Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, so no super-cap fallback is needed.","proposal":"Add Vendor IP/law/data/misconduct indemnity, mutual indemnity procedure, IP exclusions and infringement remedies (Section 20.5), and narrow the Customer indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-48c632ad","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.","rationale":"The cap is mutual but the basis is only one month of Fees actually paid — far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees and illusory against a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment (Section 2.1); \"Fees\" (Section 1.5) also excludes implementation charges, narrowing the base further. Worse, \"without exception\" overrides the Excluded Claims definition in Section 21.3, pulling indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap. The redline sets the cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and restores the Section 21.3 carve-outs as uncapped; Section 21.2 (mutual consequential-damages exclusion) and 21.3 (payment obligations not damages) already meet the playbook and are untouched.","proposal":"Raise the mutual cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and place Excluded Claims outside the cap","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-c4f0f7cf","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 already meets our preferred position in full. § 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate (as defined in § 1.1) or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, subject only to prompt notice and assignee assumption. § 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified only by capability/financial standing), and never to a direct Customer competitor. § 24.3's residual consent requirement is expressly limited to \"other assignments,\" so it does not undercut the § 24.1 carve-out. § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service on our change of control, and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. § 13.3 aligns by permitting licence transfer to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 permitted assignment. A document-wide search found no deemed-assignment trigger or other change-of-control right favouring Vendor; § 9.2 is a standard mutual insolvency right that expressly excludes lawful reorganizations. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-75577550","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","rationale":"Section 2.2 (the first of two paragraphs numbered 2.2) imposes full-term exclusive dealing on Customer for hosted analytics services, with no product-category limit, no time limit, and no performance-based exit — the playbook walk-away position. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. We therefore delete the clause to reach the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer), noting the 12-month, category-limited, SLA-terminable fallback if exclusivity is commercially necessary. No other exclusivity language binds Customer; remaining \"exclusive\" references relate to remedies and jurisdiction.","proposal":"Delete Vendor's sole and exclusive provider status (Section 2.2)","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-62b62338","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no express \"liquidated damages\" or \"penalty\" clause payable by Customer, but Section 2.1's take-or-pay commitment is functionally a Customer-payable liquidated amount: USD 2,000,000 per year for three years remains due \"without reduction or termination rights\", i.e. regardless of Services actually taken and irrespective of termination (including our convenience termination right in Section 9.4 and force-majeure termination in Section 27.3). That exposure of up to USD 6,000,000 exceeds even the walk-away threshold of remaining contract value tied to non-performance, and it contradicts Section 7.1 (no minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). Our preferred position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, so we delete the take-or-pay commitment; if a commitment is commercially essential, the fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.","proposal":"Delete the take-or-pay minimum commitment that operates as a liquidated amount payable by Customer.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-6b57f2c0","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.","rationale":"Section 13.1 is the operative Services grant and fails the rule on every parameter: it is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion (licence terminable at will), it is limited to \"Customer alone\" and expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors, and it is non-transferable. This is close to the walk-away position. Sections 13.2 (paid-up perpetual, irrevocable licence covering Affiliates and contractors) and 13.3 (transfer to Affiliate/successor; revocation only for material uncured breach after notice and cure) already reflect the preferred position, so 13.1 is internally inconsistent. The redline extends 13.1 to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, makes it transferable per 13.3, and limits revocation/suspension to the 13.3 notice-and-cure standard, which is the smallest edit reaching the preferred position without disturbing 13.2–13.4.","proposal":"Extend the Services licence to Customer's Affiliates and contractors and remove revocation at Vendor's discretion","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-953097f3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"§ 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — the playbook walk-away position. We propose the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with Fees owed only for Services ordered and actually used, leaving the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up) available in negotiation.","proposal":"Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay minimum commitment; fees payable only for Services ordered and used.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-30df7fb6","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"§ 12.4 binds Customer (Meridian) with an undefined, worldwide non-compete covering development, marketing, sale and acquisition of any competing product or service, extending 24 months post-term. That exceeds both the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer) and the walk-away threshold (post-term non-compete over 12 months / undefined \"competes with Vendor\" scope). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion; a narrowed fallback (named product, term only, ≤12 months, carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions) is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Delete § 12.4 non-compete binding Customer.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-c3725a9a","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 9.4 itself meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor is expressly denied a reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. However, Section 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment \"without reduction or termination rights,\" which directly contradicts and would gut the Section 9.4 convenience right (and any refund) for the committed volume. The order-of-precedence clause (2.2) does not resolve an internal conflict between two Agreement sections, so the ambiguity is a high-severity deviation in a multi-year term. The minimal fix conforms 2.1 to preserve the Section 9.4 right and reduce the commitment pro rata on permitted termination.","proposal":"Carve termination/reduction rights out of the take-or-pay commitment in 2.1 so the Customer convenience right in 9.4 remains effective.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-69553630","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 is the only audit right binding us and it already meets the preferred position on every parameter: frequency capped at once per twelve months (22.1); at least thirty days' prior written notice; normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption; off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1); Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and then only reasonable costs plus the undisputed shortfall (22.2). Section 22.2 also expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information, so the walk-away risks (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote system access) are absent. Section 22.3 further protects us by making findings Customer Confidential Information, limiting use to enforcement, requiring delivery of the final report, and treating payment of a shortfall as resolving the audited quantity issue. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no substantive text, so it creates no broader inspection or access right, and a full-text search found no other audit, inspection, verification, or remote-access provisions elsewhere. No redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-7f10df38","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","rationale":"Section 28.1 selects New York law and Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County, matching the preferred playbook position exactly, with a carve-out permitting either Party (including us) to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere. The Section 28.3 pre-suit executive escalation is mutual and expressly states it \"does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period,\" so it does not bar urgent relief. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-18a4f10b","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","rationale":"The IP architecture is otherwise aligned with our preferred position: 14.1 keeps all Customer Data and Customer IP with us with only a limited processing right to Vendor (reinforced by 15.1's no-sale/no-model-training limits), 14.3 leaves Vendor Technology with Vendor but pulls in the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in 13.2 for anything embedded in or required to use a Deliverable, and 14.4 bars joint ownership and protects our feedback.
